# Data quality report (generated by `src/data_quality.py`)

Source file: `data/raw/18100245.csv`. Rows: **141,432**; months **2017-01 to 2026-08**; 13 geographies; 110 products.

## 1. Missing values

- Missing prices in the full table: **34** of 141,432 rows (0.024%). Status symbols on those rows: {'..': 34}.
- Where: {'Whitehorse, Yukon': 6, 'Yellowknife, Northwest Territories': 28}.
- The two territorial capitals start in **2025-09** (StatCan note 6: added with the September 2025 release; some products suppressed for confidentiality).
- In the analysed subset (20 staples x 5 geographies, all months): **0 missing** values, months per series = [116] (expected 116), so no gaps.

## 2. Units, scale and identifiers

- Unit of measure: ['Dollars']; scalar factor: ['units']; decimals: ['2']. No unit or scale changes inside the table.
- Vectors (series IDs) per geography x product: max **1**, so no series was re-coded mid-way. `TERMINATED` flags: 0.
- **11 product names have trailing spaces** in the raw file (e.g. 'Brown rice, 900 grams ', 'Cookies and sweet biscuits, 300 grams ', 'Crackers and crisp breads, 200 grams '). They are stripped in `clean.py`; otherwise exact-name filters and joins silently miss them.
- The package size is part of the product name (e.g. `Milk, 4 litres`), so the 'unit' of each price is the product definition itself. Different sizes of the same food are separate series (milk 1 L / 2 L / 4 L; onions per kg vs 1.36 kg bag) and must not be mixed.

## 3. Product definitions

StatCan defines each product either by a **specific size** (note 3, e.g. 1 dozen eggs, prices per kg) or by a **standardized size** (note 4: packages within a size range are rescaled, e.g. 400-800 g cheese -> 500 g). Notes attached to the staples used here:

| Product | Metadata note(s) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Eggs, 1 dozen | 3 | specific size |
| Milk, 4 litres | 3 | specific size |
| Butter, 454 grams | 3 | specific size |
| Block cheese, 500 grams | 4 | standardized size |
| Whole chicken, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |
| Chicken breasts, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |
| Ground beef, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |
| Pork loin cuts, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |
| Bacon, 500 grams | 4 | standardized size |
| White bread, 675 grams | 4 | standardized size |
| White rice, 2 kilograms | 4 | standardized size |
| Dry or fresh pasta, 500 grams | 4 | standardized size |
| Wheat flour, 2.5 kilograms | 4 | standardized size |
| White sugar, 2 kilograms | 4 | standardized size |
| Roasted or ground coffee, 340 grams | 4 | standardized size |
| Canola oil, 3 litres | 4 | standardized size |
| Potatoes, 4.54 kilograms | 3 | specific size |
| Carrots, 1.36 kilograms | 4 | standardized size |
| Apples, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |
| Bananas, per kilogram | 3 | specific size |

Standardized products (cheese, bacon, coffee, pasta, bread, etc.) mix brands and package sizes, so a change in the mix that shoppers buy can move the average price even when no shelf price changed. The cube-level note 1 says it plainly: *average prices may not be fully comparable from one month to another and should not be used as a representative measure of pure price change*.

## 4. Series break: more retailers from January 2024

StatCan note 5: from the January 2024 reference month, data from **additional grocery retailers** were added. The 1-month change for January 2024 and 12-month changes during 2024 should be read with caution. Test on the staples subset (median absolute month-over-month change in January of each year):

| January of | median abs. m/m change (%) |
|---|---|
| 2018 | 3.86 |
| 2019 | 3.83 |
| 2020 | 2.93 |
| 2021 | 3.31 |
| 2022 | 3.52 |
| 2023 | 3.43 |
| 2024 | 4.3 |
| 2025 | 3.48 |
| 2026 | 2.74 |

For reference, the median absolute m/m change over all months is **3.11%**. A January 2024 value well above other Januaries would be the visible footprint of the break; see the table above for whether it shows up in these 20 staples.

## 5. Large month-over-month moves (possible outliers or composition shifts)

Moves of 20% or more in a single month in the staples subset (2017 onward): **404** of 11,500 monthly changes. Full list: `outputs/dq_large_monthly_moves.csv`. Largest:

| Month | Geography | Product | Price ($) | m/m % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2022-11 | Quebec | Potatoes, 4.54 kilograms | 4.66 | +116.7 |
| 2023-11 | Quebec | Potatoes, 4.54 kilograms | 4.62 | +90.9 |
| 2020-11 | Quebec | Potatoes, 4.54 kilograms | 4.06 | +90.6 |
| 2026-05 | Quebec | Whole chicken, per kilogram | 10.18 | +73.1 |
| 2021-11 | Quebec | Potatoes, 4.54 kilograms | 3.77 | +72.1 |
| 2022-12 | Quebec | White sugar, 2 kilograms | 2.82 | +69.9 |
| 2025-09 | Quebec | Whole chicken, per kilogram | 8.86 | +67.2 |
| 2021-04 | Quebec | Whole chicken, per kilogram | 7.55 | +66.3 |
| 2019-12 | Quebec | Whole chicken, per kilogram | 6.68 | +60.6 |
| 2026-05 | Saskatchewan | Whole chicken, per kilogram | 8.99 | +60.0 |

These were **kept** (no evidence they are errors: produce is seasonal and smaller provinces have fewer transactions), but they are a reason to prefer 12-month averages over single-month comparisons.

## 6. Unchanged values month to month

Share of months where the price is exactly equal to the previous month (to the cent): overall **4.3%**; highest for Bananas, per kilogram (34.3%). Low values are expected for scanner-data averages; a high share would suggest carried-forward (imputed) values.

## 7. Neighbouring provinces are not independent

Median absolute gap between two geographies' average prices for the same staple and month (2017 onward):

| Pair | median abs. gap (%) | months within 1% |
|---|---|---|
| Alberta vs Saskatchewan | 3.53 | 15% |
| Nova Scotia vs New Brunswick | 2.05 | 29% |
| Quebec vs Ontario | 8.43 | 7% |
| Ontario vs Alberta | 8.42 | 8% |
| Quebec vs Canada | 6.19 | 10% |

Neighbouring provinces (Prairies, Maritimes) track each other much more closely than Quebec vs Ontario. The table cannot say why (shared regional pricing by grocery chains is one plausible reason, not verified here). Practical consequence: Alberta and Saskatchewan are **not two independent data points**, so agreement between them is not treated as extra evidence.

## 8. Revisions and comparability

- Data are subject to revision (note 1). This run used the file downloaded at **2026-10-30T01:48:06Z** (UTC); re-running `src/download.py --force` may change recent months slightly.
- StatCan advises caution when comparing **across provinces** (brand/quality mix differs) and recommends the **CPI** for pure price change. This project therefore talks about *average prices paid*, not inflation in the CPI sense.
